case_title: JASWANT SINGH v. STATE OF PUNJAB & ANR.
neutral_facts: The complainant alleged that he had paid money to an individual to secure employment for his son abroad. The complainant claimed that the individual failed to fulfill the promise and that the accused did not honor their commitment, leading to the complainant's son returning after a few months. The complainant also alleged that the accused demanded additional money and threatened dire consequences if the money was not paid. The investigating officers initially found no substance in the complaint and recommended closure, but the senior superintendent of police directed the registration of an FIR. The police report concluded that a triable case was made out only against the main accused, while the other accused were exonerated. The complainant later entered into a compromise with the main accused, which was accepted by the court, leading to the closure of proceedings against the main accused. The other accused were summoned for trial, but the complainant had already settled his dispute with the main accused, and there was no justification to continue the proceedings against the other accused.
